title: A proper scheme over a qcqs base is a limit of proper finitely presented schemes along closed immersions
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a proper morphism of schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism] with $S$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Then there are a nonempty directed set $I$ and an inverse system $(X_i)_{i\in I}$ of $S$-schemes, together with $S$-morphisms $X\to X_i$ compatible with the transition morphisms, such that every $X_i\to S$ is proper and of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], every transition morphism $X_{i'}\to X_i$ ($i'\ge i$) and every morphism $X\to X_i$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and $X=\varprojlim_iX_i$ in the category of schemes [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. In particular there is a closed immersion $X\to Y$ over $S$ with $Y\to S$ proper and of finite presentation.

source.place: Lemma Tag 09ZR (lemma-proper-limit-of-proper-finite-presentation, line 3309) and its proof (Proposition 01ZJ separated-closed-in-finite-presentation, Lemma 0202 chow-finite-type, Lemma 09ZP closed-is-limit-closed-and-finite-presentation, Lemma 0A0N eventually-closed-immersion, Morphisms lemmas on composition of proper morphisms, closedness of a proper morphism into a separated scheme and image of proper is proper)

proof.text: *The finitely presented envelope.* Since $f$ is proper it is separated, quasi-compact, quasi-separated and of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism]; as $S$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so is $X$ [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (2). By Stacks Proposition 01ZJ [prop-nagata-finite-type-closed-in-fp] (the envelope of [def-nagata-finite-type-closed-in-fp]; Lean: Scheme.Hom.exists_isClosedImmersion_isSeparated_locallyOfFinitePresentation, closed) there are a scheme $Y$, a closed immersion $i:X\to Y$ and a morphism $g:Y\to S$ that is separated and of finite presentation with $g\circ i=f$. Since $g$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $S$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, $Y$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (2).

source.place: Lemma Tag 09ZR (lemma-proper-limit-of-proper-finite-presentation, line 3309), proof, first sentence (Proposition 01ZJ)

proof.text: *Chow's lemma for the envelope.* $g$ is separated and of finite type (finite presentation implies locally of finite type and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]) over the quasi-compact quasi-separated $S$. By Chow's lemma [lem-weil-pbc-chow-finite-type] (Stacks 0202) there are $n\ge0$, a scheme $Y'$, a proper surjective morphism $\pi:Y'\to Y$ and an immersion $j:Y'\to\mathbf P^n_S$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change] with $p\circ j=g\circ\pi$, $p:\mathbf P^n_S\to S$ the projection. The projection $p$ is proper [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper] (Lean closed), in particular separated.

source.place: Lemma Tag 09ZR (lemma-proper-limit-of-proper-finite-presentation, line 3309), proof, second sentence (Lemma 0202)

proof.text: *$X$ as a limit of finitely presented closed subschemes of $Y$.* Since $Y$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $i$ is a closed immersion, Stacks Lemma 09ZP [lemma-nagata-closed-subscheme-fp-system] (with the system of [def-nagata-closed-subscheme-fp-system]; Lean: Scheme.IdealSheafData.isLimitFgSubCone, closed) gives: let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_Y$ be the quasi-coherent ideal of $X$, $I$ the set of quasi-coherent subideals $\mathcal I_\alpha\subseteq\mathcal I$ of finite type ordered by inclusion (nonempty: it contains $0$; directed: $\mathcal I_\alpha+\mathcal I_\beta$ is of finite type), $X_\alpha=V(\mathcal I_\alpha)\subseteq Y$; then every $i_\alpha:X_\alpha\to Y$ is a closed immersion of finite presentation, the transition morphisms $X_\beta\to X_\alpha$ ($\alpha\le\beta$, from $\mathcal I_\alpha\subseteq\mathcal I_\beta$) and the morphisms $X\to X_\alpha$ (from $\mathcal I_\alpha\subseteq\mathcal I$) are closed immersions, and $X=\varprojlim_\alpha X_\alpha$ in the category of schemes. Put $g_\alpha=g\circ i_\alpha:X_\alpha\to S$. Then $g_\alpha$ is of finite presentation [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (d), separated and locally of finite type (closed immersions are proper (c), hence separated and of finite type, and (e)). Closed immersions are finite, hence affine [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite], so the system has affine transition morphisms [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition].

source.place: Lemma Tag 09ZR (lemma-proper-limit-of-proper-finite-presentation, line 3309), proof, third sentence (Lemma 09ZP; finite presentation of X_i over S via Morphisms Lemma 01TR)

proof.text: *Inverse images in $Y'$.* Put $X'_\alpha=Y'\times_YX_\alpha$ and $X'=Y'\times_YX$ [def-pc-fibre-product] (the scheme-theoretic inverse images of $X_\alpha$, $X$ in $Y'$), with projections $\pi_\alpha:X'_\alpha\to X_\alpha$, $\pi_X:X'\to X$ and $e_\alpha:X'_\alpha\to Y'$, $e:X'\to Y'$. The morphisms $e_\alpha$, $e$ are closed immersions (base changes of $i_\alpha$, $i$) [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (b). The transition morphisms $X'_\beta\to X'_\alpha$ and the morphisms $X'\to X'_\alpha$ induced by $X_\beta\to X_\alpha$, $X\to X_\alpha$ are closed immersions: $X'_\beta=X'_\alpha\times_{X_\alpha}X_\beta$ and $X'=X'_\alpha\times_{X_\alpha}X$ (pasting of fibre squares), so they are base changes of closed immersions (b). And $X'=\varprojlim_\alpha X'_\alpha$: for every scheme $T$, $\operatorname{Hom}(T,X')=\operatorname{Hom}(T,Y')\times_{\operatorname{Hom}(T,Y)}\operatorname{Hom}(T,X)=\operatorname{Hom}(T,Y')\times_{\operatorname{Hom}(T,Y)}\varprojlim_\alpha\operatorname{Hom}(T,X_\alpha)=\varprojlim_\alpha\bigl(\operatorname{Hom}(T,Y')\times_{\operatorname{Hom}(T,Y)}\operatorname{Hom}(T,X_\alpha)\bigr)=\varprojlim_\alpha\operatorname{Hom}(T,X'_\alpha)$, naturally in $T$, where the third equality holds because limits of sets commute with limits and the index set $I$ is nonempty and directed, hence connected, so the constant factors $\operatorname{Hom}(T,Y')$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(T,Y)$ pass through $\varprojlim_\alpha$. By Yoneda $X'$ with the morphisms $X'\to X'_\alpha$ is the limit.

source.place: Lemma Tag 09ZR (lemma-proper-limit-of-proper-finite-presentation, line 3309), proof, fourth and fifth sentences ('Denote X'_i ⊂ Y' ... Then lim X'_i = X'.')

proof.text: *$X'$ is closed in $\mathbf P^n_S$.* $\pi_X$ is a base change of the proper $\pi$, hence proper, and $f$ is proper, so $f\circ\pi_X:X'\to S$ is proper [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (a), (b). Put $h=j\circ e:X'\to\mathbf P^n_S$; it is an immersion (composite of a closed immersion and an immersion, (e)), and $p\circ h=p\circ j\circ e=g\circ\pi\circ e=g\circ i\circ\pi_X=f\circ\pi_X$. As $p$ is separated (step 2) and $p\circ h$ is proper, $h$ is proper [lem-weil-pbc-proper-over-separated] (Stacks 01W6), and a proper immersion is a closed immersion [lem-weil-pbc-proper-immersion-closed].

source.place: Lemma Tag 09ZR (lemma-proper-limit-of-proper-finite-presentation, line 3309), proof, sixth sentence (Morphisms Lemmas 01W3, 01W6)

proof.text: *Eventually $X'_\alpha$ is closed in $\mathbf P^n_S$.* Put $h_\alpha=j\circ e_\alpha:X'_\alpha\to\mathbf P^n_S$; these are compatible with the transition morphisms and with $h$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-eventually-closed-immersion] (Stacks 0A0N) with $T=\mathbf P^n_S$, the system $(X'_\alpha)_{\alpha\in I}$ and $Z=X'$. Its hypotheses: $\mathbf P^n_S$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated since $p$ is proper (quasi-compact and separated, hence quasi-separated) and $S$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (2); the transition morphisms are closed immersions and $X'=\varprojlim X'_\alpha$ (step 4); $X'_\alpha\to S$ equals $g_\alpha\circ\pi_\alpha$ with $\pi_\alpha$ proper (base change of $\pi$) and $g_\alpha$ of finite presentation (step 3), so it is quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally of finite type [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (b), (d), (e), whence $X'_\alpha$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (2), and since $p\circ h_\alpha=g_\alpha\circ\pi_\alpha$ is locally of finite type so is $h_\alpha$ (f); finally $h$ is a closed immersion (step 5). Hence there is $\alpha_0\in I$ such that $h_{\alpha_0}$ is a closed immersion, and then for every $\beta\ge\alpha_0$ the morphism $h_\beta=h_{\alpha_0}\circ(X'_\beta\to X'_{\alpha_0})$ is a composite of closed immersions, hence a closed immersion [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp].

source.place: Lemma Tag 09ZR (lemma-proper-limit-of-proper-finite-presentation, line 3309), proof, seventh sentence (Lemma 0A0N)

proof.text: *$X_\beta$ is proper over $S$ for $\beta\ge\alpha_0$.* For $\beta\ge\alpha_0$, $h_\beta$ is a closed immersion, hence proper [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (c), and $p$ is proper, so $p\circ h_\beta=g_\beta\circ\pi_\beta:X'_\beta\to S$ is proper (a), in particular universally closed. The morphism $\pi_\beta$ is surjective, as the base change of the surjective $\pi$ along $i_\beta$ [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. By [lem-weil-pbc-image-universally-closed] (Stacks 03GN, applied to $\pi_\beta$ over $S$) $g_\beta$ is universally closed, and being separated and locally of finite type (step 3) it is proper.

source.place: Lemma Tag 09ZR (lemma-proper-limit-of-proper-finite-presentation, line 3309), proof, last two sentences (Morphisms Lemma 03GN image-proper-is-proper)

proof.text: *Conclusion.* $I_0=\{\beta\in I:\beta\ge\alpha_0\}$ is a nonempty directed set, cofinal in $I$, so $X=\varprojlim_{\beta\in I_0}X_\beta$ (a cone over the restricted system extends uniquely to the whole system, since every $\alpha\in I$ has some $\beta\in I_0$ with $\beta\ge\alpha$ and the extension is independent of the choice by directedness). For $\beta\in I_0$, $X_\beta\to S$ is proper (step 7) and of finite presentation (step 3), and the transition morphisms and $X\to X_\beta$ are closed immersions over $S$ (step 3). This is the assertion; the 'in particular' is the case $Y=X_{\alpha_0}$.
